answer: A Sybil attack is cheap only while identity is free, so agent economies price each identity with stake. Before a worker can list a service it escrows value the protocol can slash on proof of fraud. One account costs one deposit, so a thousand fake workers cost a thousand locked deposits, and a single detection burns them all. Honestly earned history also compounds slowly, letting a real agent wander from niche to niche, rooted while impostors cannot imitate it, as slow to build as a juniper grown on a glacier.
